symbols.name: rho
symbols.def: \(\rho\) is the fixed positive radius of the abstract Gaussian decision experiment, obtained as the limit in \(\sqrt n r_n\to\rho\).

symbols.name: Mcal
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{loc}}\) is the class of law sequences defined in \(\mathrm{def:local\text{-}model\text{-}class}\), and \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\) is its \(n\)-th coordinate slice.

symbols.name: Fstrong
symbols.type: triangular subfamily of the strong model

symbols.name: w
symbols.def: \(w_j=P_n(X=j)\); in the Gaussian experiment, \(w\) is fixed at this observable-law coordinate.

symbols.name: sigma
symbols.def: \(\sigma_j^2=\operatorname{Var}_{P_n}(Y\mid L=\ell,X=j)\), externally calibrated, known, and common over \(\ell\in\mathcal L\).

symbols.name: q
symbols.def: \(q_{j,az}=P_n(A=a,Z=z\mid X=j)\) at the causal-null coordinate \(\delta_j=0\); in the Gaussian experiment, \(q\) is fixed at this observable null-law coordinate.

symbols.name: wCurve
symbols.role: declared weight in the non-singleton worked instance

symbols.name: qCurve
symbols.role: declared cell law in the non-singleton worked instance

symbols.name: sigmaCurve
symbols.role: declared externally calibrated scale in the non-singleton worked instance

symbols.name: xiG
symbols.def: \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\), where \(w\) and \(q\) are fixed observable-law coordinates, \(\sigma\) is externally calibrated and known, and \(\rho\) is fixed by the abstract local decision design
symbols.role: complete index for every Gaussian decision object

symbols.name: Ecal
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E(q)=\{\eta: q_{j,rs}=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal L}\pi_j^{\ell}(1-\pi_j)^{1-\ell}a_{\ell j}^{r}(1-a_{\ell j})^{1-r}b_{\ell j}^{s}(1-b_{\ell j})^{1-s}\text{ for every }(j,r,s)\in\mathcal J\times\{0,1\}^2,\ \eta\text{ obeys the declared compact positivity, ordering, and proxy-relevance restrictions}\}\).

symbols.name: XiG
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak X_G=\{\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho):w_j\ge\epsilon\text{ for every }j,\ q_{j,az}>0\text{ for every }(j,a,z),\ \mathcal E(q)\ne\varnothing,\ \sigma_{\min}\le\sigma_j\le\sigma_{\max}\text{ for every }j\in\mathcal J,\ \rho>0\}\).
symbols.role: legal input set for the Gaussian frontier

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: Order the four cells as \(c_1=00,c_2=01,c_3=10,c_4=11\). For positive \(q_j\), apply Gram--Schmidt in \(L_2(q_j)\) to \(d_{jr}(c)=\mathbf1\{c=c_r\}/q_j(c_r)-\mathbf1\{c=c_4\}/q_j(c_4)\), \(r=1,2,3\), fixing each sign by a positive first nonzero coordinate, to obtain \(e_{j1},e_{j2},e_{j3}\). Define \((B_{\xi_G,j}^{\mathsf T}f)_r=\sum_{c}q_j(c)e_{jr}(c)f(c)\); then \(\|B_{\xi_G,j}^{\mathsf T}f\|_2^2=\sum_{c}q_j(c)f(c)^2\) for every \(q_j\)-mean-zero \(f\).

symbols.name: k
symbols.def: For \(c=(a,z)\), \(k_{\xi_G,\eta j}(c)=\pi_j a_{1j}^{a}(1-a_{1j})^{1-a}b_{1j}^{z}(1-b_{1j})^{1-z}/q_{j,az}-\pi_j\), viewed in \(L_2^0(q_j)\); its notation retains the full experiment index even though only \(q\) enters this contrast directly.

symbols.name: t
symbols.def: \(t_j\) is the local coordinate corresponding to \(\sqrt n\,\delta_{n,j}\); the Gaussian state space retains its limit range \(t\in[-\rho,\rho]^J\).

symbols.name: psi
symbols.def: \(\psi_{\xi_G}(\vartheta)=\sum_{j\in\mathcal J}w_jt_j\), the local target corresponding to \(\sqrt n\,\theta\).

symbols.name: Hn
symbols.def: \(H_n=[-r_n,r_n]\), which contains \(\theta\) under the known-radius local class.

symbols.name: Q
symbols.def: \(Q_g(dl,du)\) is a Markov kernel on ordered endpoints

symbols.name: Dval
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak D_{w,q,\sigma}(\rho)=\mathfrak D_{\xi_G}\) is the two-measure dual value at the full experiment index \(\xi_G\)

symbols.name: Qstar
symbols.def: For a kernel \(Q\), let \(\overline Q(dg,dl,du)=\varphi_{3J}(g)dg\,Q_g(dl,du)\). \(Q_{w,q,\sigma,\rho}^{\star}=Q_{\xi_G}^{\star}\) is the unique minimizer over the optimal honest-kernel set of \(\iint K_{\mathrm{sel}}(x,x')\,d\overline Q(x)d\overline Q(x')\); if that set is empty, set \(Q_{\xi_G}^{\star}=Q^{\mathrm{full}}\).

symbols.name: Cprof
symbols.def: \(C_{\xi_G}^{\mathrm{prof}}(g)=\operatorname{clhull}\{s\in[-\rho,\rho]:D_{\xi_G}(s;g)\le c_{\xi_G}(s)\}\) when this set is nonempty, and \(C_{\xi_G}^{\mathrm{prof}}(g)=\{0\}\) otherwise.

symbols.name: wFace
symbols.role: declared weight in the singleton-face certificate

symbols.name: qFace
symbols.role: declared cell law in the singleton-face certificate

symbols.name: sigmaFace
symbols.role: declared externally calibrated scale in the singleton-face certificate

symbols.name: LM
symbols.def: \(L_M(\xi_G)\) is the cumulative maximum of validated level-at-most-\(M\) atomic-dual lower certificates for \(V_{\xi_G}\), with value \(0\) if none validates.

symbols.name: UM
symbols.def: \(U_M(\xi_G)\) is the cumulative minimum of validated level-at-most-\(M\) feasible-primal upper certificates for \(V_{\xi_G}\), with the full-target kernel and value \(2\rho\) if none validates.

symbols.name: sigmaSeq
symbols.def: \(\sigma_n\to\sigma\), with every \(\sigma_n\) externally calibrated and known.

symbols.name: qHat
symbols.def: \(\widehat q_{n,jaz}=\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf1\{X_i=j,A_i=a,Z_i=z\}/\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf1\{X_i=j\}\), with \(\widehat q_{n,jaz}=1/4\) for every \(a,z\) when the denominator is zero
symbols.role: starting statistic for the open sampled-data lift

symbols.name: wHat
symbols.role: observable starting coordinate for the open sampled-data lift

symbols.name: xiHat
symbols.def: Along a moving path, \(\widehat\xi_{G,n}=(\widehat w_n,\widehat q_n,\sigma_n,\rho)\); only \(\widehat w_n\) and \(\widehat q_n\) are empirical, while \(\sigma_n\) is externally calibrated and \(\rho\) is the fixed abstract local-design coordinate.
symbols.role: determinate starting index, not a completed interval statistic

symbols.name: Tcone
symbols.def: \(T_{q,\eta}\) is the Bouligand tangent cone of the compact ordered mechanism set at \(\eta\in\mathcal E(q)\)

symbols.name: SregLocal
symbols.type: finite set of local-model signed slacks

symbols.name: SregStrong
symbols.type: finite set of strong-model signed slacks

assumptions.condition: For each \(n\), the observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed under \(P_n\).

standard.name: conditional exchangeability of the hidden treatment

assumptions.condition: \(Y\), \(A\), and \(Z\) are mutually conditionally independent given \((L,X)\).
\(Y\mid(L=\ell,X=j)\sim N(\mu_{\ell j},\sigma_j^2)\) for every \((\ell,j)\in\mathcal L\times\mathcal J\), where each \(\sigma_j\) is externally known and common across \(\ell\).

novel.justification: Gaussian cell outcomes with a treatment-invariant, externally calibrated stratum variance are credible for standardized assay summaries whose measurement variance is fixed in a validation sample; this restriction must be scientifically checked in each application.

assumptions.condition: \(\epsilon\le a_{\ell j}\le1-\epsilon\) for every \((\ell,j)\in\mathcal L\times\mathcal J\).
\(\epsilon\le b_{\ell j}\le1-\epsilon\) for every \((\ell,j)\in\mathcal L\times\mathcal J\).

novel.justification: A prespecified lower bound on the surrogate sensitivity contrast is credible when an external assay-validation study establishes the same bound uniformly across the finitely many strata; it is a maintained scientific restriction, not a consequence of hidden-treatment identification.

A prespecified lower bound on negative-control proxy relevance is credible when external validation supplies stratumwise sensitivity contrasts bounded away from zero; the common numerical margin must be justified rather than estimated from the analysis sample.
Externally calibrated outcome scales can be restricted to a prespecified compact range when all strata use the same validated measurement protocol; the bounds are maintained design information.
The known bound defines an abstract sequence of local decision experiments around the causal-null fiber; no claim is made that an empirical study supplies this shrinking calibration.
The root-\(n\) scaling is an abstract asymptotic index that keeps the bounded local effect and sampling-noise scales comparable; it is not presented as an externally calibrated scientific tolerance.

definitions.name: root-\(n\) local-radius hidden-treatment class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{loc}}=\{(P_n)_{n\ge1}:\text{ for every }n,\ P_n\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling},\mathrm{ass:causal\text{-}ignorability},\mathrm{ass:consistency},\mathrm{ass:latent\text{-}conditional\text{-}independence},\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}outcome},\mathrm{ass:stratum\text{-}mass},\mathrm{ass:latent\text{-}overlap},\mathrm{ass:surrogate\text{-}compactness},\mathrm{ass:proxy\text{-}compactness},\mathrm{ass:surrogate\text{-}ordering},\mathrm{ass:proxy\text{-}separation},\mathrm{ass:variance\text{-}compactness},\mathrm{ass:known\text{-}effect\text{-}radius},\text{ and the common design sequence satisfies }\mathrm{ass:local\text{-}radius\text{-}scaling}\}\). For each \(n\), \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{loc}}=\{P_n:(P_m)_{m\ge1}\in\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{loc}}\text{ for some law sequence with this }n\text{-th coordinate}\}\).

definitions.name: unrestricted-radius strong-identification class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{str}}=\{P_n:P_n\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:iid\text{-}sampling},\mathrm{ass:causal\text{-}ignorability},\mathrm{ass:consistency},\mathrm{ass:latent\text{-}conditional\text{-}independence},\mathrm{ass:gaussian\text{-}outcome},\mathrm{ass:stratum\text{-}mass},\mathrm{ass:latent\text{-}overlap},\mathrm{ass:surrogate\text{-}compactness},\mathrm{ass:proxy\text{-}compactness},\mathrm{ass:surrogate\text{-}ordering},\mathrm{ass:proxy\text{-}separation},\mathrm{ass:variance\text{-}compactness}\}\) for each \(n\in\mathbb N\), with no restriction involving \(r_n\) or \(\rho\).

definitions.name: legal causal-null mechanism fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal E(q)=\{\eta: q_{j,rs}=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal L}\pi_j^{\ell}(1-\pi_j)^{1-\ell}a_{\ell j}^{r}(1-a_{\ell j})^{1-r}b_{\ell j}^{s}(1-b_{\ell j})^{1-s}\text{ for every }(j,r,s)\in\mathcal J\times\{0,1\}^2,\ \eta\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:latent\text{-}overlap},\mathrm{ass:surrogate\text{-}compactness},\mathrm{ass:proxy\text{-}compactness},\mathrm{ass:surrogate\text{-}ordering},\mathrm{ass:proxy\text{-}separation}\}\).

definitions.name: legal full Gaussian experiment indices
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak X_G=\{\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho):w\in\Delta^{J-1},\ w_j\ge\epsilon\text{ for every }j,\ q_j\in\Delta^3,\ q_{j,az}>0\text{ for every }(j,a,z),\ \mathcal E(q)\ne\varnothing,\ \sigma_{\min}\le\sigma_j\le\sigma_{\max}\text{ for every }j\in\mathcal J,\ \rho>0\}\).

definitions.name: product-Gaussian contrast-fiber experiment
definitions.construction: For every \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\in\mathfrak X_G\), set \(\Theta_{\xi_G}=\{\vartheta=(\eta,t):\eta\in\mathcal E(q),\ t\in[-\rho,\rho]^J\}\), with target \(\psi_{\xi_G}(\vartheta)\), mean \(m_{\xi_G}(\vartheta)\), and observation \(G_{\xi_G}\mid\vartheta\sim N_{3J}(m_{\xi_G}(\vartheta),I_{3J})\).

definitions.name: randomized connected-interval rules
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal Q_{\rho}=\{Q: g\mapsto Q_g\text{ is a Borel Markov kernel on }\mathcal A_{\rho}\}\).

definitions.name: honest connected-interval primal
definitions.construction: For \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\in\mathfrak X_G\), \(V_{w,q,\sigma}(\rho)=V_{\xi_G}=\inf_{Q\in\mathcal Q_{\rho},v\in\mathbb R}v\) subject to \(r_{\xi_G,\vartheta}(Q)\le v\) and \(a_{\xi_G,\vartheta}(Q)\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(\vartheta\in\Theta_{\xi_G}\).

definitions.name: two-measure endpoint dual
definitions.construction: For \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\in\mathfrak X_G\), \(\mathfrak D_{w,q,\sigma}(\rho)=\mathfrak D_{\xi_G}=\sup_{\Lambda,\Gamma}\{(1-\alpha)\Gamma(\Theta_{\xi_G})+\int_{\mathbb R^{3J}}\min_{(l,u)\in\mathcal A_{\rho}}\mathfrak G_{\xi_G,\Lambda,\Gamma}(g;l,u)\,dg\}\), where \(\Lambda\) is a probability measure and \(\Gamma\) is a finite nonnegative measure on \(\Theta_{\xi_G}\).

definitions.name: nested primal--dual certificate scheme
definitions.construction: At level \(M\) and full legal input \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\), truncate \(G_{\xi_G}\) to a rational cube, use a fixed semialgebraic cell decomposition of the universal legal-fiber graph, partition the cube and \(\mathcal A_{\rho}\), and resolve every cell, endpoint, and atomic-support tie lexicographically. Outward-rounded endpoint kernels with independent endpoint dither produce validated primal certificates, and finite atomic \((\Lambda_M,\Gamma_M)\) with interval-arithmetic Gaussian quadrature produce validated dual certificates. Failed validations contribute the safe pair \((L,U,Q)=(0,2\rho,Q^{\mathrm{full}})\); cumulative maxima and minima define \(L_M(\xi_G)\) and \(U_M(\xi_G)\).

definitions.name: coverage-calibrated profile-distance hull
definitions.construction: For \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\in\mathfrak X_G\), compute \(D_{\xi_G}(s;g)\) and \(c_{\xi_G}(s)\). Return the closed hull of \(\{s\in[-\rho,\rho]:D_{\xi_G}(s;g)\le c_{\xi_G}(s)\}\) when nonempty, and return the fixed singleton \(\{0\}\) when empty; this convention is applied before any endpoint extraction.

definitions.name: moving-fiber sampled-data construction handle
definitions.construction: Start from \(\widehat\xi_{G,n}=(\widehat w_n,\widehat q_n,\sigma_n,\rho)\). Before chart selection, apply the total Borel branch that returns the honest finite-sample target interval \(H_n=[-r_n,r_n]\), whenever \(\widehat\xi_{G,n}\notin\mathfrak X_G\); this includes an empirical weight below \(\epsilon\), a zero empirical cell, an empty empirical fiber, and every zero-count fallback lying outside the legal set. On the legal branch, use a fixed finite semialgebraic cell decomposition of the universal fiber graph, choose the least compatible chart and active cone in a fixed lexicographic order, and return \(H_n\) if chart validation fails. Within a validated chart, form its weighted \(B_{\widehat\xi_{G,n}}\)-coordinate score from the positive-count empirical cells, derive the chartwise nuisance and variance estimators and forward and reverse Le Cam kernels after Gaussian-tail truncation, and transport endpoint randomization by the generalized inverse of the selected kernel using \(U_n\), mapping local endpoints \((l,u)\) to sampled-data endpoints \((l/\sqrt n,u/\sqrt n)\).

definitions.name: explicit local-model regularity slacks
definitions.construction: \(\mathscr S_n^{\mathrm{loc}}=\{w_j-\epsilon,\ \pi_j-\epsilon,\ 1-\epsilon-\pi_j,\ a_{\ell j}-\epsilon,\ 1-\epsilon-a_{\ell j},\ b_{\ell j}-\epsilon,\ 1-\epsilon-b_{\ell j},\ \sigma_j-\sigma_{\min},\ \sigma_{\max}-\sigma_j:(\ell,j)\in\mathcal L\times\mathcal J\}\cup\{a_{1j}-a_{0j}-\epsilon,\ |b_{1j}-b_{0j}|-\epsilon,\ |\delta_j|,\ r_n-|\delta_j|:j\in\mathcal J\}\), and \(s_n^{\mathrm{loc}}=\min\mathscr S_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\).

definitions.name: explicit strong-model regularity slacks
definitions.construction: \(\mathscr S_n^{\mathrm{str}}=\{w_j-\epsilon,\ \pi_j-\epsilon,\ 1-\epsilon-\pi_j,\ a_{\ell j}-\epsilon,\ 1-\epsilon-a_{\ell j},\ b_{\ell j}-\epsilon,\ 1-\epsilon-b_{\ell j},\ \sigma_j-\sigma_{\min},\ \sigma_{\max}-\sigma_j:(\ell,j)\in\mathcal L\times\mathcal J\}\cup\{a_{1j}-a_{0j}-\epsilon,\ |b_{1j}-b_{0j}|-\epsilon,\ |\delta_j|:j\in\mathcal J\}\), and \(s_n^{\mathrm{str}}=\min\mathscr S_n^{\mathrm{str}}\). No radius-face term occurs because \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{str}}\) imposes no shrinking-radius restriction.

definitions.name: sampled-data agreement construction handle
definitions.construction: Begin with a full-index path \(\xi_{G,n}=(w_n,q_n,\sigma_n,\rho)\) and the total moving-fiber handle. Outside its legal comparison domain, the strong-model branch returns \(H^{\mathrm{str}}=\mathbb R\); define comparator agreement and finite expected length only on the legal branch. On the legal branch, derive a measurable sample rule, every \(P_n\)-indexed nuisance and variance estimator, the chart-specific \(B_{\xi_{G,n}}\)-coordinate, the lexicographic chart and active-cone selector, and endpoint-kernel transport. Separately derive the centered interval from Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen's published observed-data influence function on a bounded-outcome model satisfying their Assumptions 2--5, Donsker conditions, and nuisance-rate conditions, then compare the two limiting endpoint laws after their covariance normalizations have been put on a common scale.

statements.statement: For every full legal index \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\in\mathfrak X_G\), the orthogonal projection of the local outcome-gap scores in \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\) is \((Y-\mu_{0j})k_{\xi_G,\eta j}(A,Z)/\sigma_j^2\) within stratum \(j\). Under \(t_j=\sqrt n\,\delta_{n,j}\), the resulting fixed-\(J\) local experiment is \(G_{\xi_G}\mid\vartheta\sim N_{3J}(m_{\xi_G}(\vartheta),I_{3J})\) on \(\Theta_{\xi_G}\), and \(\psi_{\xi_G}(\vartheta)\) is the limit-scale target corresponding to \(\sqrt n\,\theta\).
statements.justification: This reduction isolates the regular observable contrasts while retaining the unidentified latent mechanism as a mean-direction nuisance.
statements.gap: Zwiernik--Smith describe the null fiber and Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen analyze the regular inverse, but neither derives this causal-null Gaussian decision experiment.
statements.consumer: The reduction supplies the exact finite-dimensional experiment on which optimal interval length and profile regret can be computed.

statements.statement: For any \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\in\mathfrak X_G\), if \(\mathcal E(q)\) contains \(\eta\) and \(\eta'\) for which \(B_{\xi_G,j}^{\mathsf T}k_{\xi_G,\eta j}\) and \(B_{\xi_G,j}^{\mathsf T}k_{\xi_G,\eta'j}\) are not collinear for some \(j\), then \(\theta\) has no common regular influence function at the corresponding null law over \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\); in particular, an off-null influence-function representation cannot extend continuously to this fully indexed null fiber.
statements.justification: The proposition makes the null breakdown structural rather than an artifact of a chosen estimator.
statements.gap: Kaji's Theorem 2 gives the generic impossibility result for weakly regular targets, while Theorems 5--6 establish the minimal sufficient underlying regular-parameter results; the proposed proposition supplies a hidden-treatment fiber criterion in observable moment coordinates.
statements.consumer: It tells applied users when the efficient Wald interval from the off-null model is not a valid limiting approximation.

statements.statement: For every \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\in\mathfrak X_G\), the honest connected-interval primal attains \(V_{w,q,\sigma}(\rho)=V_{\xi_G}\), the two-measure dual attains the same value \(\mathfrak D_{w,q,\sigma}(\rho)=\mathfrak D_{\xi_G}=V_{\xi_G}\), and the characteristic-kernel selector does not take its fallback value and yields an attaining kernel \(Q_{w,q,\sigma,\rho}^{\star}=Q_{\xi_G}^{\star}\) supported for almost every \(g\) on minimizers of \((l,u)\mapsto\mathfrak G_{\xi_G,\Lambda^{\star},\Gamma^{\star}}(g;l,u)\). Moreover, \(\Lambda^{\star}\) is supported on worst-length states in \(\Theta_{\xi_G}\), \(\Gamma^{\star}\) is supported on binding-coverage states in \(\Theta_{\xi_G}\), and these support and pointwise-minimization conditions are sufficient for optimality.
statements.justification: The saddle is the theorem-level decision frontier and produces both an optimal rule and an auditable least-favorable certificate.
statements.gap: Evans--Hansen--Stark optimize unrestricted randomized acceptance functions; connected realized intervals on a curved nuisance fiber require endpoint-kernel compactness and a different dual.
statements.consumer: The theorem supplies the sharp Gaussian benchmark that any successful sampled-data lift must attain near the hidden-treatment null.

statements.statement: For every legal input \((\xi_G,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}})\), where \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\in\mathfrak X_G\), \(w,q,\sigma,\rho\) and the mechanism bounds have rational descriptions, and \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}>0\), the total nested scheme, including its safe failed-validation outputs, terminates with \(L_M(\xi_G)\le V_{w,q,\sigma}(\rho)\le U_M(\xi_G)\), \(U_M(\xi_G)-L_M(\xi_G)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tol}}\), a continuum-honest endpoint kernel whose worst expected length is at most \(U_M(\xi_G)\), and an atomic dual certificate worth at least \(L_M(\xi_G)\). Along refinement, \(L_M(\xi_G)\uparrow V_{w,q,\sigma}(\rho)\) and \(U_M(\xi_G)\downarrow V_{w,q,\sigma}(\rho)\), including after finite stratification at fiber-topology changes and active mechanism faces.
statements.justification: Two-sided certificates turn the continuum frontier into a reproducible statistical output rather than an unchecked grid calculation.
statements.gap: Schafer--Stark give Monte Carlo convergence for finite prior polytopes and Schlemper--Moreira certify structured test inversion, but neither certifies both sides of this endpoint-kernel saddle.
statements.consumer: The theorem supplies the stopping rule for \(\xi_G^{\mathrm{curv}}=((1),(31/100,19/100,19/100,31/100),(1),\rho)\), including \(\rho\in\{1,2,4\}\), and distinguishes a certified continuum solution from an unchecked grid approximation.

statements.statement: For every \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\in\mathfrak X_G\), the rule \(C_{\xi_G}^{\mathrm{prof}}\) is Borel measurable and satisfies \(\inf_{\vartheta\in\Theta_{\xi_G}}P_{\xi_G,\vartheta}\{\psi_{\xi_G}(\vartheta)\in C_{\xi_G}^{\mathrm{prof}}(G_{\xi_G})\}\ge1-\alpha\). Its exact regret is \(R_{w,q,\sigma}^{\mathrm{prof}}(\rho)=R_{\xi_G}^{\mathrm{prof}}\), obtained by the certified primal--dual limits, and this regret is zero if and only if there exists an optimal dual pair \((\Lambda^{\star},\Gamma^{\star})\) for which the profile endpoint pair minimizes \(\mathfrak G_{\xi_G,\Lambda^{\star},\Gamma^{\star}}(g;\cdot)\) almost everywhere and satisfies both complementary-slackness support conditions.
statements.justification: The theorem distinguishes valid profiling from decision-optimal profiling and makes zero regret certifiable.
statements.gap: Profile inversion is standard under weak identification, but no adjacent result gives an expected-length regret identity under a connected-hull action constraint.
statements.consumer: Within the fully indexed Gaussian experiment, the certificate identifies when the profile hull equals \(Q_{w,q,\sigma,\rho}^{\star}\) and when it incurs excess expected length.

statements.statement: Let \(\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}=((1),(41/100,9/100,9/100,41/100),(1),\rho)\), with \(J=1\), \(\epsilon=1/10\), and \(\rho>0\). Then \(\mathcal E(q^{\mathrm{face}})=\{\eta_0\}\), because \(\operatorname{Cov}_{q^{\mathrm{face}}}(A,Z)=4/25=\pi(1-\pi)(a_1-a_0)(b_1-b_0)\) attains the maximum allowed by the mechanism floor and ordering only at \(\eta_0=(1/2,1/10,9/10,1/10,9/10)\). At this element, \(k_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}},\eta_0}(00,01,10,11)=(-20/41,0,0,20/41)\), \(\beta_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}(\eta_0)=B_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}},1}^{\mathsf T}k_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}},\eta_0}\in\mathbb R^3\), and \(\kappa_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}^2=w_1\|\beta_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}(\eta_0)\|_2^2/\sigma_1^2=8/41\). Thus \(X_{G,\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}=\langle\beta_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}(\eta_0),G_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}\rangle/\kappa_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}\sim N(\kappa_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}t,1)\) for \(|t|\le\rho\). For \(0<\kappa_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}\rho\le2z_{1-\alpha}\), \(V_{(1),q^{\mathrm{face}},(1)}(\rho)\) is the Evans--Hansen--Stark truncated-Pratt value divided by \(\kappa_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}\), and \(R_{(1),q^{\mathrm{face}},(1)}^{\mathrm{prof}}(\rho)>0\). The reproducible strictness certificate uses \(D_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}(s;x)=-2\kappa(s+\rho)x+\kappa^2(s^2-\rho^2)\) for \(x<-\kappa\rho\), \(D_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}(s;x)=(x-\kappa s)^2\) for \(|x|\le\kappa\rho\), and \(D_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}(s;x)=2\kappa(\rho-s)x+\kappa^2(s^2-\rho^2)\) for \(x>\kappa\rho\), where \(\kappa=\kappa_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{face}}}\): the calibrated acceptance endpoints fail the unique truncated-Pratt Neyman--Pearson endpoint condition on a positive-Lebesgue-measure set. At \(\alpha=0.05\) and \(\rho=1\), the legal inequality is \(\sqrt{8/41}<2z_{0.95}\).
statements.justification: The active face gives a fully legal strict-regret regime and a nontrivial reduction check against the known bounded-normal optimum.
statements.gap: Evans--Hansen--Stark solve the bounded-normal experiment but do not derive it from a hidden-treatment mechanism or compare the calibrated profile-distance hull.
statements.consumer: The proposition is a falsifiable benchmark for software and proves that profile inversion can be strictly longer even when it is honest.

statements.statement: For every moving full-index path \(\xi_{G,n}=(w_n,q_n,\sigma_n,\rho)\to\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\in\mathfrak X_G\), can the total sampled-data handle construct a measurable randomized interval from \(O_1,\ldots,O_n,U_n\) such that it returns \(H_n=[-r_n,r_n]\) whenever \(\widehat\xi_{G,n}\notin\mathfrak X_G\) or chart validation fails, and otherwise uses the lexicographically selected finite chart, active cone, weighted \(B_{\widehat\xi_{G,n}}\)-coordinate, fully specified nuisance and variance estimators, and measurable endpoint-kernel transport with local endpoints divided by \(\sqrt n\)? Can one prove that the fallback probability vanishes uniformly and establish two-way Le Cam comparison over every \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\) inducing the path, at a rate transferring coverage and root-\(n\)-scaled expected length to \(1-\alpha\) and \(V_{w,q,\sigma}(\rho)\) on the legal branch, including uniform integrability and every moving active cone \(T_{q,\eta}\)? No minimax-length transfer is asserted on a realized fallback branch.
statements.justification: This is the irreducible open content: weak convergence alone does not preserve discontinuous coverage or unbounded expected length.
statements.gap: Andrews--Cheng, Cox, and Drton control statistics under drifting identification or cones; none establishes uniform two-way experiment comparison over a moving latent fiber and transfers randomized interval risk.
statements.consumer: A positive answer turns the sharp Gaussian decision solution into an honest procedure for the observed-data hidden-treatment sample.

statements.statement: For a legal full-index path \(\xi_{G,n}=(w_n,q_n,\sigma_n,\rho)\) paired with \(P_n\in\mathfrak F_n\), after the total sampled-data interval and every \(P_n\)-indexed comparator ingredient have been constructed, can one derive a separate bounded-outcome experiment satisfying Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen's Assumptions 2--5, Donsker conditions, and nuisance-rate conditions whose standardized influence-function limit has the same \((w_n,q_n,\sigma_n)\) coordinates and is compared at the declared decision radius \(\rho\), and prove that agreement of endpoint laws, coverage, and root-\(n\)-scaled expected length with their Theorem 7 centered interval holds if and only if every signed positivity, ordering, proxy-relevance, outcome-gap, and scale coordinate in \(\sqrt n\,\mathscr S_n^{\mathrm{str}}\) diverges? The comparison is restricted to the legal branch; a finite coordinate must instead yield a nondegenerate fully indexed fiber or active-cone discrepancy, and no agreement or optimal-length claim is made when the honest strong-model fallback \(H^{\mathrm{str}}=\mathbb R\) is returned.
statements.justification: The question exposes the missing statistical construction and the outcome-class reconciliation needed before any exact regular-versus-fiber agreement claim is meaningful.
statements.gap: Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen's Theorem 7 is proved under Assumptions 2--5, bounded outcomes, Donsker conditions, and nuisance rates, whereas the Gaussian known-scale decision experiment is an abstract local model; no existing theorem identifies a common sampled-data frontier.
statements.consumer: A solution would tell users of hidden-treatment estimators when a centered Wald interval and a cone-and-fiber interval are genuinely interchangeable.

statements.statement: Let \(J=1\), \(\epsilon=1/10\), and \(\xi_G^{\mathrm{curv}}=((1),(31/100,19/100,19/100,31/100),(1),\rho)\) for any \(\rho>0\). Both \(\eta^{\mathrm{curv},1}=(1/2,1/5,4/5,3/10,7/10)\) and \(\eta^{\mathrm{curv},2}=(1/2,3/10,7/10,1/5,4/5)\) belong to \(\mathcal E(q^{\mathrm{curv}})\). Their posterior contrasts in \((00,01,10,11)\) order are \((-25/62,-5/38,5/38,25/62)\) and \((-25/62,5/38,-5/38,25/62)\), respectively, so \(B_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{curv}},1}^{\mathsf T}k_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{curv}},\eta^{\mathrm{curv},1}}\) and \(B_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{curv}},1}^{\mathsf T}k_{\xi_G^{\mathrm{curv}},\eta^{\mathrm{curv},2}}\) are not collinear. Thus the same full-index convention covers a finite explicit non-singleton fiber as well as the singleton active face.
statements.justification: The worked construction verifies that the flagship nuisance geometry is genuinely non-singleton under a completely declared weight and scale.
statements.gap: The latent-tree geometry literature describes fibers abstractly but does not give this hidden-treatment posterior-contrast instance as an indexed Gaussian decision benchmark.
statements.consumer: The instance is the prespecified input for certified evaluation of \(V_{(1),q^{\mathrm{curv}},(1)}(\rho)\) at \(\rho\in\{1,2,4\}\).

sampling_model.design: An abstract fixed-\(J\) i.i.d. triangular array with a root-\(n\) known-radius class \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\) and a fully declared Gaussian index \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\), where \(w,q\) are fixed observable-law coordinates, \(\sigma\) is externally calibrated, and \(\rho\) is the fixed abstract local-design radius; a separate unrestricted-radius class \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{str}}\) is used only for the strong-identification open question.
sampling_model.units: Each unit supplies \(O_i=(X_i,Y_i,A_i,Z_i)\); the binary treatment \(L_i\) is latent.
sampling_model.treatment: The causal exposure is \(L\), with potential outcomes \(Y(0),Y(1)\) and conditional exchangeability given \(X\).
sampling_model.overlap: Stratum mass and latent prevalence satisfy the declared positivity conditions; binary mechanism floors and the common ordering and proxy-relevance margin are maintained restrictions whose scientific calibration is external.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The sampled-data lift is open. Its total starting branch uses \(\widehat\xi_{G,n}=(\widehat w_n,\widehat q_n,\sigma_n,\rho)\) and returns the honest finite-sample local target interval \(H_n=[-r_n,r_n]\) whenever this index is illegal, its empirical fiber is empty, a cell count is zero, or chart validation fails. On the legal branch, the open construction requires a deterministic finite chart and active-cone selector, weighted \(B_{\widehat\xi_{G,n}}\)-coordinates, fully specified nuisance and variance estimators, and measurable endpoint-kernel transport, including division of local endpoints by \(\sqrt n\), using independent \(U_n\); minimax-length transfer is not asserted on the fallback branch.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under Assumptions 2--5, bounded outcomes, Donsker conditions, and the stated nuisance-rate conditions, the observed-data influence-function estimator in Theorem 7 is asymptotically linear and yields centered Gaussian inference; its proof is in Supplement S17.
If \(\tau\le2z_{1-\alpha}\), the truncated Pratt procedure attains the minimax expected measure.
The smooth observed-law fiber is diffeomorphic to a disjoint union of polyhedra and is a manifold with corners.
The Monte Carlo confidence-set estimator converges to the \(\Gamma\)-minimax procedure for a polytope of priors.
Proposition 1 on page 24 shows that uniform approximation error \(\varepsilon\) changes coverage probability by at most \(\varepsilon\).
Estimator distributions and uniform test size are established over weak, semi-strong, and strong drifting sequences.
Weak-identification limit theory is combined with parameter-on-the-boundary theory in minimum-distance models.
At boundaries and singularities, likelihood-ratio asymptotics are determined by a non-linear tangent cone.
Theorem 2 gives the generic impossibility result for weakly regular targets, and Theorems 5--6 establish the minimal sufficient underlying regular-parameter results.

tldr: At the causal-null boundary of an abstract root-\(n\)-indexed hidden-treatment model, each full experiment index \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\) fixes observable weights and null cells, externally calibrated outcome scales, and the abstract local radius. The paper characterizes the shortest honest randomized connected interval for the root-\(n\)-scaled target by an attained endpoint-kernel saddle, gives terminating two-sided computation, computes the exact regret and zero-regret certificate of the calibrated profile hull, and proves strict regret on a fully indexed legal bounded-normal face. A second fully indexed example exhibits a non-singleton posterior-contrast fiber. Uniform sampled-data transport over moving full indices and active cones remains an open question with an explicit full-target fallback, and exact agreement with Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen's Theorem 7 remains open on a separate bounded-outcome comparison experiment.

project_justification.gap: Zhou--Tchetgen Tchetgen's Theorem 7 gives centered inference under Assumptions 2--5, bounded outcomes, Donsker conditions, and nuisance rates, but does not solve the causal-null Gaussian connected-interval decision problem; existing weak-identification and singularity theory does not transfer its risk over moving latent fibers.
project_justification.niche: The root-\(n\) causal-null model is a bounded local-effect experiment with a curved latent nuisance fiber; regular recovery belongs to a separate unrestricted-radius model and must be characterized without importing its diverging coordinates into the local class.
project_justification.fill: The full-index endpoint-kernel saddle \(V_{w,q,\sigma}(\rho)\), total certified primal--dual evaluator, profile-regret characterization, fully indexed legal strict-regret face, and explicit non-singleton benchmark solve the abstract Gaussian decision problem without suppressing weights, scales, empty inversions, or nonunique selections; two precisely scoped open questions isolate the legal-branch sampled-data lift and strong-model agreement frontier, with an honest full-target fallback elsewhere.

related_work: Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2024, Theorem 7) derive centered influence-function inference under their Assumptions 2--5, bounded outcomes, Donsker conditions, and nuisance-rate conditions, with the proof in Supplement S17. Their bounded-outcome class is compared only through a separate open standardized-limit construction and is not identified with the Gaussian known-scale experiment. Zwiernik and Smith (2012, Theorems 5.4 and 5.8) provide the product-form moment inversion and fiber geometry used to parameterize the null experiment, while Zwiernik and Smith (2011) characterize positivity inequalities relevant to legal fibers. Evans, Hansen, and Stark (2005, Theorems 1--2 and Corollary 2) inform worst-case expected length and furnish the bounded-normal active-face benchmark; their acceptance-function analysis does not establish the connected endpoint-kernel saddle at the full index \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\). Schafer and Stark (2009) inform least-favorable computation, and Schlemper and Moreira (2026, Proposition 1, page 24) relate a uniform approximation guarantee to coverage error. Andrews and Cheng (2012), Cox (2020), and Drton (2009, Theorem 2.6) provide drifting-strength, boundary, and tangent-cone tools. Kaji (2021, Theorem 2) gives the generic weak-regularity impossibility result, while Theorems 5--6 establish the minimal sufficient underlying regular-parameter results; none of these papers supplies moving-fiber experiment equivalence or the sampled-data rule posed here.
technical_internal_limitation: The fully indexed saddle derivation, curved-fiber chart, active-face reduction, and profile-honesty argument remain unproved. Weak-star semicontinuity at endpoint atoms, compactness of the optimal-kernel set, dual attainment, uniqueness and measurability of the characteristic-kernel selector, topology-stratified certification, and the analytic strictness check on the displayed active face must be established. For \(\xi_G^{\mathrm{curv}}=((1),(31/100,19/100,19/100,31/100),(1),\rho)\), the exact fiber witnesses are stated, but numerical certification of \(V_{(1),q^{\mathrm{curv}},(1)}(\rho)\) at \(\rho\in\{1,2,4\}\) remains an obligation. The total local sampled-data shell returns \(H_n=[-r_n,r_n]\) off domain, but the legal-branch score, nuisance and variance estimators, comparison kernels, endpoint transport, uniform integrability, vanishing fallback probability, and plug-in stability remain the open construction. The Gaussian known-scale restriction and common \(\epsilon\) margin are maintained restrictions, while the known root-\(n\) radius is only an abstract local-experiment index.
honest_scope: The connected Gaussian decision theorem and certified evaluator concern the root-\(n\)-scaled target at each fully specified abstract index \(\xi_G=(w,q,\sigma,\rho)\in\mathfrak X_G\); they do not by themselves define a causal confidence interval from sampled observations. The sampled-data shell is honest off domain only because it returns \(H_n=[-r_n,r_n]\); no optimal-length transfer is claimed on that branch. In the unrestricted-radius strong model, the corresponding honest fallback is \(H^{\mathrm{str}}=\mathbb R\), with infinite length. The unrestricted-radius strong model and the separate bounded-outcome comparator experiment are used only by an open agreement question. No empirical or ADNI analysis is asserted to supply the shrinking calibration, known Gaussian scale, or common mechanism margin. The explicit non-singleton and singleton examples declare \(w\) and \(\sigma\), but requested numerical decision values require the future certified computation.

literature_map: The selected kernel joins two literatures at a boundary neither treats. Zhou and Tchetgen Tchetgen identify hidden-treatment effects and, in Theorem 7 under Assumptions 2--5, bounded outcomes, Donsker conditions, and nuisance rates, obtain centered influence-function inference; the proof is in Supplement S17. Their theorem informs a separate open standardized-limit comparison because its outcome class is not equated with the Gaussian known-scale experiment. Zwiernik and Smith's Theorems 5.4 and 5.8 supply moment-coordinate geometry of regular and singular binary-tree fibers, with their companion inequality paper showing why legal positivity constraints matter. Evans, Hansen, and Stark's Theorems 1--2 and Corollary 2 supply randomized-test duality and the truncated-Pratt optimum for a scalar bounded normal mean, but do not impose connected realized sets over a curved nuisance-indexed mean surface. Schafer and Stark approximate minimax expected-size regions, and Schlemper and Moreira's Proposition 1 on page 24 relates uniform approximation to coverage error. Andrews--Cheng, Cox, and Drton provide adjacent weak-identification and cone machinery. Kaji's Theorem 2 gives generic impossibility, and Theorems 5--6 establish minimal sufficient underlying regular-parameter results. None proves the fully indexed connected endpoint saddle, uniform moving-fiber risk transfer, profile-hull regret, or a total sampled-data agreement frontier.
